HEATING / PRACTICAL ENERGY GUIDE

How much does a space heater cost to run?

A 1,500 W electric space heater costs $0.24 per hour at an example rate of $0.16/kWh. Four hours of full-power operation per day comes to $28.80 over 30 days.

Illustrative figures · USD · Replace the example rate with your own

Calculate the hourly cost

Convert the electrical input from watts to kilowatts, then multiply by your electricity price. For a heater drawing a steady 1,500 W:

1,500 ÷ 1,000 × $0.16 = $0.24 per hour

At four hours per day, the heater uses 6 kWh daily. Multiply $0.24 by 4 to get $0.96 per day, then by 30 to get $28.80 for a 30-day period. Enter 0.16 in the calculator for 16 cents per kWh.

This covers the heater's energy use. Fixed utility charges, taxes, and other appliances are additional.

Compare daily running time

Illustrative 1,500 W heater at $0.16/kWh, running continuously at full power
Daily running timeDaily energyDaily cost30-day cost
1 hour1.5 kWh$0.24$7.20
2 hours3 kWh$0.48$14.40
4 hours6 kWh$0.96$28.80
8 hours12 kWh$1.92$57.60

For example, reducing full-power operation from four hours to three hours per day reduces this estimate by $7.20 over 30 days. This is an arithmetic comparison, not a prediction of your heating needs.

Compare power settings

Illustrative input power levels, each running 4 hours/day at $0.16/kWh
Electrical inputHourly cost30-day cost
500 W$0.08$9.60
1,000 W$0.16$19.20
1,500 W$0.24$28.80

Use the power draw for the setting you actually select. Lower power for longer can use the same energy: 750 W for eight hours and 1,500 W for four hours both use 6 kWh. Compare total energy over the same period.

Account for thermostat cycling

A heater with a thermostat may stop drawing its heating power after reaching the set temperature. Four hours switched on does not necessarily mean four hours at full power.

Suppose a 1,500 W heater's heating element runs for two of those four hours. The heating-element estimate becomes 1.5 × 2 × $0.16 = $0.48 per day, or $14.40 over 30 days. Controls or a fan may consume additional energy.

If you measure average power across the entire session, multiply that average by the whole session length. If you use rated heating power, enter the equivalent full-power hours. Do not apply the same on/off adjustment twice.

Make the estimate your own

  1. Read the electrical input on the heater label or manual for your chosen setting.
  2. Find your variable electricity rate per kWh on your bill.
  3. Estimate actual heating time, or use measured average consumption.
  4. Choose your billing period and compare the result with measured use.

There is no single space-heater cost that applies to every home. The heater's setting, operating time, and your electricity price determine this calculation.
